executive_summary.headline: Describe an idea and get a working tool
executive_summary.body: Meta's Muse Spaces builds custom tools from a description, and Zuckerberg says he used it to track his smoker's temperature. Perplexity Teammates and ChatGPT's GIF maker point the same way: standing agents and one-prompt creations.

executive_summary.headline: Creators chain a coding agent to a creative tool
executive_summary.body: Roberto Nickson cuts a 15-second story from 15 clips by prompting Muse inside Edits. Morrow Studio and Andries Ohneisser pair Claude with Blender and video models to make 3D shorts and floor-plan walkthroughs.

executive_summary.headline: Autonomous labs now publish hard numbers
executive_summary.body: Nature's AutoDNA ran 11,000+ steps across 20+ instruments with humans only refilling reagents, and Anthropic's 207,049-session study shows scientists use AI least for ideation.

top_picks.title: Roberto Nickson cuts a 15-second trip story from 15 clips with one prompt to Muse inside Edits
top_picks.summary: Roberto Nickson says Muse, driving the new Edits desktop app over MCP, took 15 videos from a Trip folder, picked the best second from each and sequenced a 15-second story with a trending song that fits the footage. His clip shows the run sped up 5X. Edits for Mac is free, adds a multi-track timeline, keyframes and 4K export without a watermark, and publishes straight to Instagram, per Digital Trends.
top_picks.author: @rpn (Roberto Nickson)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand an editing app to an agent and describe the cut in one sentence. Fun way to try it: point it at a folder of last weekend's photos and ask for a 15-second highlight reel with a song that matches the mood.

secondary_urls.label: Digital Trends: Edits comes to Mac

top_picks.why_it_matters: The prompt is the whole workflow: folder in, finished story out. It is the clearest demo this week of an agent operating a creative app instead of just writing about it.

top_picks.title: Muse Spaces turns a described idea into a custom tool, and Zuckerberg builds a smoker controller with it
top_picks.summary: Mark Zuckerberg says he used the new Spaces feature in Muse to build a tool for his smoker, and that Muse now tracks the temperature through the day after the vent controller gained Bluetooth. Meta's announcement says you describe an idea and Muse builds a custom tool, with examples such as a holiday gift tracker, wedding planner, client hub for freelancers and an order tracker for a small business. Spaces is available wherever Muse is available from Nov 6.
top_picks.author: Mark Zuckerberg (@zuck)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: describe the small tool you keep wishing existed and let the assistant build it as a shareable space. Fun way to try it: build a gift tracker for the next holiday and share it with the family.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Muse was the most-posted tool in this week's Threads sample, and Spaces is the feature behind most of those posts.

top_picks.title: Andries Ohneisser chains Claude Opus 5.5, Blender, Seedream 5 Pro and Seedance 2.5 to turn a floor plan into a video walkthrough
top_picks.summary: Ohneis cites NAR's survey figure that 57% of US home buyers call floor plans very useful, then describes a four-step build: Opus 5.5 rebuilds the house in Blender, one camera path runs through the rooms, Seedream 5 Pro sets each room's look as a still, and Seedance 2.5 follows that exact path. The post describes the pipeline; it does not publish a finished-video benchmark.
top_picks.author: Andries Ohneisser (@ohneis652)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: fix the camera path in 3D first, then let the video model restyle each room along it. Fun way to try it: sketch your own home's floor plan and generate a walkthrough in three different decor styles.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Fixing geometry before styling keeps rooms consistent, which is the usual failure of prompt-only walkthroughs. Useful for anyone showing spaces, products or building layouts.

top_picks.title: Morrow Studio shows Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and Blender building 'How It's Built' 3D Shorts
top_picks.summary: Morrow Studio's 9:42 tutorial, posted Nov 4, walks through using Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and Blender to produce 3D explainer Shorts from a kit. The description says one video in this format passed 30 million views, and the channel reports 64 Shorts with 35.4 million views across two TikTok accounts from Oct 5 to 26. The channel states those are its own results, not typical. The tutorial itself had 165 views at fetch time.
top_picks.author: Morrow Studio
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let a coding agent drive a 3D tool to make short explainers from a repeatable template. Fun way to try it: animate how your favorite everyday object is built, one part per second.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A repeatable format plus a published kit makes this a recipe, not a showreel. The view totals are the channel's own claims.

top_picks.title: AutoDNA, an AI-native lab, runs 11,000+ steps across 20+ instruments with humans only refilling reagents
top_picks.summary: Nature published AutoDNA from Shanghai Jiao Tong University on Nov 4. The lab orchestrates more than 20 instrument types over more than 11,000 steps covering DNA synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing. It matched expert-optimized enzymatic synthesis yields, ran concurrent protocols 3.2 times faster, completed an end-to-end DNA data-storage cycle with exact recovery, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. Chosun reports 11,382 steps over 203 hours.
top_picks.author: Shanghai Jiao Tong University team
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: make every instrument callable by one scheduler and let the humans only restock. Fun way to try it: map the five steps of your most repeated routine and mark which ones a machine could run unattended.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Science bonus: autonomous lab with hard numbers (3.2x concurrent speedup, exact data recovery) from a peer-reviewed journal.

top_picks.title: Anthropic's study of 207,049 research sessions shows scientists use AI most for data analysis and writing, least for ideation
top_picks.summary: Anthropic's Nov 5 study covers 207,049 research sessions on consumer plans from Aug 2 to Sep 30, plus a survey of 528 scientists. Use is highest for data analysis and writing and lowest for ideation and gathering, although scientists rank ideation first in importance. Under wide adoption, Anthropic estimates AI could take on 27 to 52% of the researcher time needed for a new study, median 38%. Those are scenario estimates, not observed savings.
top_picks.author: Anthropic
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: find the stage of your work where people want help most and use it least, then build a tool for that gap. Fun way to try it: rank your own week's tasks by importance and by AI use, and look for the biggest mismatch.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Science bonus: shows where researchers actually use AI today versus where they say it matters most, with a clear gap at ideation.

top_picks.title: Personal Finance in Claude links accounts and answers spending questions in a US beta
top_picks.summary: Anthropic's release notes dated Nov 5 describe a beta that lets users link bank, credit card, loan and investment accounts to see balances and spending on one page and ask questions about their money. It is available on Pro, Max and Ultra plans in the US only. TechCrunch adds that it connects through Plaid, can flag duplicate charges and rising bills, and reads up to two years of transactions.
top_picks.author: Anthropic
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an assistant plain questions about your own statements instead of building a spreadsheet. Fun way to try it: ask what your three fastest-growing subscriptions were last quarter.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A mainstream assistant moves from chat into a personal-data workflow people already do by hand.

sections.title: LinkedIn
sections.description: Voices and creator tooling from LinkedIn this week. Post pages were not reachable, so these come from the authors' own sites and press.

items.title: Andrew Ng: a LinkedIn Pulse study counts 2 million jobs created by AI, and embedded AI engineers now pay off
items.summary: Andrew Ng's Nov 6 letter cites LinkedIn data that AI has helped create 2 million jobs and that AI Engineer is among the 10 fastest-growing jobs in seven major economies. He argues that coding agents make it practical to embed an AI-savvy engineer in marketing, HR or finance to build workflow automations, dashboards and custom apps.
items.author: Andrew Ng
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pair one builder with a non-engineering group for a month. Fun way to try it: have the pair automate the dullest weekly report and demo it on Friday.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: draft by hand first, brainstorm alone, then bring in Claude
items.summary: In a Nov 6 interview, Ethan Mollick says he types every first draft himself and brainstorms alone before opening Claude. He adds that AI fact-checked his new book, Co-Intelligence: The Next Phase of AI, and found errors in cited papers.
items.author: Ethan Mollick
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: write the first pass yourself, then use AI as the fact-checker. Fun way to try it: run your last published piece through a model and count the errors it finds.

items.title: LinkedIn adds an exportable Post Performance Table for creators
items.summary: LinkedIn announced a consolidated analytics view on Nov 3 that lists per-post impressions, members reached, watch time, followers gained, saves and sends, with export. NetInfluencer reports it is global on desktop.
items.author: LinkedIn (Sam Corrao Clanon)
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: export per-post metrics and ask an assistant which formats earn saves and sends. Fun way to try it: feed the last 30 posts to a model and ask it to name the one pattern you repeat.

sections.title: TikTok
sections.description: Trends and creator builds, read through third-party trackers because TikTok blocks automated reads.

items.title: 'First Time in a Fancy Cafe' becomes the week's AI video template
items.summary: A dev.to comparison covers four ways to make the trend, including a CapCut template and a Fancy Cafe AI app at $3.99 for a 10-second 480p clip built on Seedance 2.0. Trend tracker jumponthetrend shows Kevin Winnik's version posted Nov 2 and a @leehoustonx version at 7.8M views and 1M likes by Nov 3.
items.author: Yining Lin (dev.to); trend data from jumponthetrend
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a trend is a prompt you can reuse with your own subject. Fun way to try it: make the fancy-cafe clip with your pet as the first-time guest.
items.why_it_matters: Counts come from a third-party tracker; TikTok itself blocks automated reads.

items.title: @viralex.aii shows Claude Code editing video and reaches 562K views
items.summary: Virlo's tracker lists a Nov 3 TikTok from @viralex.aii on using Claude Code for AI video editing at 562K views.
items.author: @viralex.aii
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let a coding agent do the cutting while you describe the edit. Fun way to try it: ask it to trim a long clip to the three funniest seconds.

items.title: @l2ueducation automates email receipts with no code
items.summary: The same Virlo page lists a Nov 5 TikTok from @l2ueducation on a no-code email-receipt automation, at 54K views.
items.author: @l2ueducation
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: route receipts from your inbox into a sheet automatically. Fun way to try it: set it up for one month and see the total you actually spent on coffee.

items.title: AI-made character @jean_philanthrope reaches 284,900 followers and 4M likes across 10 videos
items.summary: A Nov 2 press release from Hermoso says its AI-made character account @jean_philanthrope has 284,900 followers and 4M likes from 10 videos, and announces character recasting. The figures are the company's own.
items.author: Hermoso
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give a recurring character a consistent face and voice, then recast the same script. Fun way to try it: create a character for your family chat and have them narrate the weekly plan.

sections.title: Instagram
sections.description: Creator editing tools arriving on desktop and the web.

items.title: Edits for Mac is free, with a multi-track timeline, keyframes, color wheels and watermark-free 4K export
items.summary: Instagram's @creators account announced Edits for desktop on Nov 5. Digital Trends reports the Mac app runs on Apple-silicon Macs, adds a multi-track timeline, keyframes and color wheels, exports 4K with no watermark and publishes straight to Instagram.
items.author: Instagram (@creators)
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give a free editor to everyone who makes short video and see what they build. Fun way to try it: recut your last Reel with keyframes on a single title.
items.recurrence_note: Last week's Instagram item was the Features long-video test; this week's evidence is a free pro-grade editor for the same creator audience.

items.title: Instagram adds Reels templates, trending effects and in-browser editing
items.summary: TechShots reports on Nov 8 that Reels gains templates, trending effects and editing in a web browser. The page does not mention AI features.
items.author: TechShots
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: start from a template that already fits the trend. Fun way to try it: remake one old clip in a trending template and compare the reach.

sections.title: Facebook and Meta
sections.description: Muse in the hands of small businesses and creators.

items.title: April Polk and Tom Mulholland use Muse to run a shoe shop and a grocery
items.summary: Salena Zito's Nov 3 column says April Polk of JaeLuxe Shoetique had Muse expand a two-page brand guide to 12 pages, fix duplicate email flows and rebuild her website in about half an hour. Tom Mulholland of Mulholland Grocery in Malvern, Iowa photographs the wholesaler's catalog pages and employee timecards, and Muse prepares the weekly ad, totals payroll hours and posts to Facebook and Instagram.
items.author: Salena Zito
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: photograph the paperwork and let the assistant total, draft and post. Fun way to try it: snap this week's receipts and ask for a one-paragraph recap of the week.

items.title: Meta's creator assistant on Facebook sends trend alerts and drafts storyboards in the creator's voice
items.summary: Social Media Today reports Nov 2 that Meta's creator assistant now gives proactive trend alerts, builds a storyboard and shot list, gives feedback on drafts and replies to comments in the creator's voice. It is on the web through Creator Dashboard.
items.author: Meta
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an assistant for the shot list before you press record. Fun way to try it: have it storyboard a 30-second video about your hobby.

items.title: Muse video chat through an animated avatar opens to everyone in the US
items.summary: TechCrunch reports on Nov 5 that Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar.
items.author: Meta
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: put a face and voice on an assistant so people talk to it like a colleague. Fun way to try it: rehearse a presentation out loud with the avatar as the audience.

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Autonomous labs, open models and adoption data from researchers.

items.title: AI agents design and run a robot lab, writing 200+ commands for a robotic arm
items.summary: Nature news on Nov 6 covers an arXiv preprint in which AI agents simulated a virtual lab and then wrote more than 200 commands for a robotic arm to measure nanocrystal optical properties. The preprint is not peer reviewed.
items.author: Nature
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: rehearse in a simulated lab before touching hardware. Fun way to try it: have an agent write the steps for a kitchen recipe in a simulator first.
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus: agents plan and execute physical experiments.

items.title: A Y Combinator startup puts $1M behind five open materials-science problems for AI
items.summary: TechCrunch reports on Nov 5 that Discovered Materials has a $1M prize pool for five open problems. Frontier models with internet access worked autonomously for days on each problem and made little headway.
items.author: Discovered Materials
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: post a prize-backed open problem and let anyone's agent try it. Fun way to try it: set a small bounty for a puzzle in your own group.
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus: materials discovery challenge with a real prize pool.

items.title: Deep Principle releases open-weight Hydrogen-1.0 for chemistry and materials
items.summary: A Nov 6 release from Deep Principle says Hydrogen-1.0, post-trained from GLM-5.3, is on Hugging Face and ModelScope. Examples include a 12-vial Suzuki coupling protocol revised after a virtual rehearsal and a GROMACS polyethylene workflow. The details are the company's own.
items.author: Deep Principle
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: rehearse a protocol virtually, then run it. Fun way to try it: have a model plan a recipe batch and revise it before you cook.
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus: open weights for chemistry and materials work.

items.title: 10x Genomics CTO: coders have adopted AI, experimentation is 'extremely niche'
items.summary: R&D World reports on Nov 5 that the CTO says the vast majority of coders have adopted AI while use in actual experimentation is extremely niche. The adoption tactic is to let scientists use the tool as much or as little as they want, with no full switch required.
items.author: 10x Genomics CTO
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: offer the tool with no mandate and let the early users show the rest. Fun way to try it: start a show-and-tell where each person demos one thing they tried.

sections.title: Creators, Indies and Small Business
sections.description: New tools and numbers from solo builders and small teams.

items.title: CNBC profiles owners who run companies with no employees using AI
items.summary: CNBC reports on Nov 7 that Alex Willen runs 12 e-commerce brands with no employees and expects $2.5M to $3M in revenue, and Kristin Ginn made roughly $250K in about 7 months on under $60 a month of AI tools. Gusto data cited shows AI adopters' headcount is about 7% higher.
items.author: CNBC
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: write one-person processes as checklists an agent can run. Fun way to try it: automate one repeating task for a side project this week.

items.title: Playful lets non-coders make and share web apps from a few prompts
items.summary: Fast Company reports on Nov 5 that Playful, from Mike Harrington and Darrin Massena, builds web apps and games from a few prompts that users can put on their phones and share. Two apps are free for 30 days, then $10 a month.
items.author: Jared Newman
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: make building an app as social as posting a photo. Fun way to try it: build a tiny quiz for your friends and send the link.

items.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 makes animated GIFs from a prompt or photo
items.summary: TNW reports on Nov 4 that ChatGPT can make GIFs from a prompt or photo with speed and frame editing, rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users. API models are GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst.
items.author: TNW
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn a photo into a looping reaction. Fun way to try it: animate a photo of your desk chair spinning for the group chat.

items.title: Perplexity Teammates are always-on agents that take on ongoing jobs
items.summary: Perplexity's Nov 5 post says Teammates take on jobs and work proactively using Computer tasks, skills, memory and tools, and can message coworkers in Slack. It is available now for Max subscribers on the web. Engadget adds iOS and the $200 a month Max price.
items.author: Perplexity
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: assign an agent a standing job instead of a one-off prompt. Fun way to try it: hand it a weekly reading list and ask for a Friday summary.

items.title: Claude shows people using Opus 5.5 to learn how jet engines and electromagnetic fields work
items.summary: Claude's Nov 6 Threads post asks what is inside a jet engine and how electromagnetic fields work, and shares what people are building with Claude Opus 5.5 to understand how things work.
items.author: Claude (@claudeai)
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: have a model build an interactive explainer of a machine. Fun way to try it: ask for a clickable model of how your coffee maker works.

items.title: Google highlights what builders made with Gemini 4 Argon three weeks after rollout
items.summary: Google's Nov 6 post says developers and creators have used Gemini 4 Argon's deep reasoning and visual capabilities for ambitious projects and shares favorites. Gemini's updates page dates the Argon rollout to Oct 13 for Google AI Pro and Ultra.
items.author: Google (@google)
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: publish a gallery of what users built. Fun way to try it: share your three favorite builds this month with one line each.

emerging_signals.pattern: Personal agents are becoming app builders
emerging_signals.evidence: Muse Spaces, Perplexity Teammates and ChatGPT's new GIF maker all take a description and return a working artifact. Muse was the most-mentioned tool in our Threads sample with 15 posts.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether Spaces are shared between people, as the client-hub and family examples suggest.

emerging_signals.pattern: Creators chain a coding agent to a 3D, video or editing tool
emerging_signals.evidence: Edits through MCP (Nickson), Claude Code plus Blender (Morrow Studio), and Claude plus Blender, Seedream and Seedance (Ohneisser) appeared in the same week.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether MCP connectors ship for more editors beyond Edits.

emerging_signals.pattern: Autonomous labs and adoption tactics move together
emerging_signals.evidence: AutoDNA, the Nature robot-lab preprint, the Discovered Materials prize and the 10x Genomics 'as much or as little as you want' approach all landed Nov 4 to 6.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether open models such as Hydrogen-1.0 get used in the five Discovered Materials problems.

emerging_signals.pattern: No-employee and solo businesses publish numbers
emerging_signals.evidence: CNBC profiles owners with 12 brands and no staff, and two Muse small-business owners describe payroll and ad workflows.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether more solo owners post their monthly tool cost next to revenue.

suggested_refinements.notes: Access limits: LinkedIn post pages for the window were unreachable (sign-in walls); TikTok blocks automated reads, so TikTok figures come from third-party trackers; Instagram reel pages dated after Oct 31 were not indexed, so Instagram items rely on Threads posts and press; Facebook video pages were not usable.
